newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Kingfisher set for profit boost.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Kingfisher set for profit boost.

text.p: British retailer Kingfisher Plc is expected to raise profits by about 30 percent when it reports annual results next Wednesday.

The firm, whose B&Q chain is UK market leader in DIY, is forecast to make pre-tax profits in the year to January 1997 of between 376.0 and 380.1 million stg, up from 287.2 million in the previous 12 months. The dividend is expected to rise to between 17.9 to 18.5 pence, from 16.2 pence.

Analysts were confident of a strong performance after the firm's upbeat trading statement on Christmas sales. In January Kingfisher reported a 7.8 percent increase in like-for-like sales over the nine weeks to January 4.
"Their Christmas trading statement was the best of the bunch," said one retail analyst, who said there could be some upgrades if electricals chain Comet, Woolworths and B&Q maintained their momentum.
Forecasts for the current year are around the 430 million stg mark.

There are some concerns that current trading may have slowed down because of a weaker trend in general retail sales and there are also worries about the performance of Darty, the French electricals retailer, in a sluggish French economy.
Kingfisher's shares, trading at a modest premium to the FTSE All-Share index, have been buffeted by takeover speculation in the past week.

The firm was rumoured to be a target for a bid from French retail conglomerate Pinault-Printemps Redoute, and also the front-runner for the purchase of Littlewoods trademark stores, put up for sale last week.

Analysts were sceptical about the likelihood of a Pinault bid. On Littlewoods, they said Kingfisher was more likely to make an aquisition in continental Europe at the durables end of the market than buy Littlewoods.

"The rationale is that Kingfisher's Chartwell Land would buy the Littlewoods sites and lease the ground floors to Tesco," said one retail analyst, but he said Kingfisher was not his favourite to buy the stores.

Kingfisher already has a 26 percent stake in French furniture and electricals retailer BUT, which has prompted speculation it might buy the entire group. The retailer, which has to wait until 1998 before making any offer, has declined to comment on its intentions. --Jane Merriman, London Newsroom + 44 171 542 7717
